newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia to set London Club agreement date July - MoF.
newsitem.headline: Russia to set London Club agreement date July - MoF.

text.p: The Russian government will set the date for signing a rescheduling agreement with the London club of commercial bank creditors in July, a senior Finance Ministry official said.

Vneshekonombank, Russia's government agent on foreign debt, said last week it had acknowledged about 80 percent of banks' claims and that creditors had returned signed reconciliation statements for just under 20 percent of eligible debt.

Russian Deputy Finance Minister Mikhail Kasyanov told Reuters in a weekend interview that Russia had asked creditors to sign reconciliation statements, at least in part, on the sums which they agreed on, in order to increase the total volume of debt so far reconciled.
"By the end of June or start of July Vneshekonombank will finish reconciling the remaining sum and then we can count on creditors approving the remaining sum during July," Kasyanov said.
"By mid-July there will come a moment when we shall have every reason to set the signing date so that the exact closing date can be calculated," Kasyanov said.
The agreement, made in principle two years ago, sketched plans for repayment of $25.5 billion of principal over 25 years and $7 billion in overdue interest over 20 years.
Russia must reconcile a minimum of $20 billion in order to close the London Club agreement.
